checks.finding: requirements.md:171 requires accepting a child that has already completed when expiry is checked. acceptance-tests.md:60 instead requires unconditional success for a stub exiting at approximately the two-second deadline, across at least five iterations. Approximate timing does not establish whether completion preceded the expiry decision; a legitimate timeout can therefore fail this test. Implementers and verifiers cannot agree on the expected result without inventing an ordering rule. This is a Major specification-level acceptance ambiguity. Define the observable completion-before-expiry condition and require the fixture to establish that ordering.

investigation.md:70-79 records that check-cross-model exits 2 when no verdict files exist, while investigation.md:83-95 quotes the existing policy declaring exit 1 for that same condition. requirements.md:145 requires executable evidence that documentation and behavior match, but BL-002 at requirements.md:183 forbids changing the gate and BL-003 at requirements.md:184 preserves the meaning of that policy passage. These obligations cannot all be satisfied for an empty verdict set. An implementer must violate either behavior/documentation equality or a preservation constraint. This belongs to specification review because the conflicting obligations require a scope decision, and is Critical under the calibration for contradictory goals. Explicitly authorize the applicable policy correction or revise the equality obligation and document the exception.

AC-003 at requirements.md:49 requires unset and empty configuration to select an effective timeout of 600 seconds. TEST-003 at acceptance-tests.md:38-41 asserts only that those inputs invoke the CLI; TEST-012 at acceptance-tests.md:122 derives an expected default from source without specifying an assertion that either fallback branch actually uses it. A runner that accepts unset/empty values but disables its deadline could satisfy the stated assertions, while TEST-004 exercises only explicit timeout values. This is a Major missing acceptance assertion for required configuration branches, within specification review rather than a request for implementation details. Require observable verification of the effective default for both unset and empty inputs.

BL-005 at requirements.md:186 relies on current PROTECTED_GATE_SUFFIXES membership to conclude that no human-copy staging applies; investigation.md:150-166 supplies the historical membership evidence. requirements.md:178 defers citation re-verification until implementation start, but gives no instruction to re-verify this shared registration surface at review time, when the no-staging conclusion is consumed. Under the supplied project rule WFI-013, this is a Major structural gap: reviewers and task authors could rely on obsolete membership to choose the wrong workflow. Require review-time re-verification and explicitly condition the staging conclusion on its result. The guard list was not read because it is outside this invocation's allowed inputs.

Implementation-policy review would have to resolve product and acceptance decisions left open by requirements.md:145,183-184 and acceptance-tests.md:60: which exit-code promise governs the empty-verdict case, and which completion ordering requires success at the timeout boundary. These are the independently evidenced CONTRADICTION and AMBIGUITY findings, not missing architecture or task details. They block handoff because a design reviewer would otherwise invent or override required behavior; severity Major.
